planting.note: Soak seed overnight before sowing into cool, moist soil; Bravour tolerates hard freezes well enough to be sown for an overwintering crop in mild climates.

directions: Bravour is a European moss-curled parsley that earned the RHS Award of Garden Merit for its dense, tightly ruffled, dark green foliage and reliable garden performance. Its compact, uniform habit and exceptional cold tolerance make it a dependable choice for spring, summer, and overwintered plantings alike. Harvest outer leaves regularly to keep the tight rosette producing tender new growth, and expect it to hold color and flavor through several hard frosts before finally succumbing to deep winter cold.

planting.note: Soak seed overnight to speed slow germination; sow into cool, moist soil in early spring for a tall, showy stand of curled foliage.

directions: Paramount is an older American curled parsley bred for dense, thick, triple-ruffled leaves on plants noticeably taller than most curly types, giving it a bold, upright presence as a border or edging plant as well as a kitchen herb. The heavy curl holds up well as a plate garnish while still delivering good fresh parsley flavor for cooking. Because the plants grow tall and full, space them slightly wider than compact curly cultivars and harvest outer stems regularly to keep new curled growth coming from the crown.

common_name: Jim Best Oregano (Trailing Golden Marbled Oregano)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown starts after the last hard frost in well-drained soil; site where afternoon shade can reach the foliage, since leaf marbling is most vivid when plants are shielded from the hottest midday sun.

directions: Jim Best is an ornamental selection of common oregano prized for its gold-and-green marbled foliage on lax, trailing stems that spill attractively over the edge of a container or raised bed. Leaf variegation is most pronounced when plants get some relief from intense afternoon sun, making it a good candidate for a partly shaded herb pot or hanging basket rather than a full-sun bed. Unlike purely ornamental oregano hybrids, its leaves retain usable oregano flavor, though it is grown primarily for foliage color and trailing habit. Trim stem tips periodically to keep growth dense and prevent the trailing stems from becoming sparse and leggy.
